answer: A durable defense is to make identity expensive to fake but cheap to verify: agents earn reputation only after completing verifiable work on a public ledger, and the score decays if they go idle. A newcomer must bridge its history from an established network instead of starting fresh, so a Sybil farmer cannot spin up thousands of clean slates overnight. Treat reputation like ivory - rare, hard to carve, easy to inspect - while the wider nebula of unverified newcomers stays sandboxed, able to observe but not transact until proven.
